label: VERIFIED
extraction: Anthropic decision framework for when to use multi-agent systems. Multi-agent architecture: multiple LLM instances with separate conversation contexts coordinated through code. Orchestrator-subagent pattern: hierarchical model where lead spawns and manages specialized subagents. Key findings: teams invest months building elaborate multi-agent architectures only to discover improved prompting on single agent achieved equivalent results. Common failure: lost context at each handoff, spent more tokens coordinating than executing. Multi-agent provides value when addressing specific constraints single agent cannot overcome: 1) Single agent accumulates everything in context (must reason about technical issue while maintaining 20+ files), 2) Parallel workstreams with independent context, 3) Specialization single agent can't sustain. Managed infrastructure can handle orchestration (Claude Managed Agents). Patterns: generator-verifier, orchestrator-subagent, agent teams. Principle: reserve multi-agent for cases with clear benefits justifying cost.
